name: Untere Isar & Karwendelschlucht
kurzbeschreibung: The pristine Untere Isarklamm (Gleirschklamm) near Scharnitz enchants hikers with emerald pools and a dramatic, wild gorge in the Karwendel.
preis: Free of charge (Länd car park in Scharnitz requires parking fee)
oeffnungszeiten: Safely accessible from mid-May to late October (closed in winter)
beschreibung:
Overview

The pristine Untere Isarklamm (also known on hiking maps as the Gleirschklamm) is a hidden gem tucked inside the Karwendel Nature Park near Scharnitz. Not far from the source of the River Isar, the crystal-clear Gleirschbach torrent cuts through towering limestone cliffs, creating an untouched, wild gorge of extraordinary alpine beauty. Unlike heavily commercialised show gorges, this ravine has retained its completely authentic, natural character. Churning pools, natural rockfalls, emerald basins, and dense mountain forests characterise this strictly protected habitat. Hikers will discover an oasis of tranquility far removed from tourist crowds, surrounded by the soothing murmur of rushing mountain water and the aromatic scent of mountain pines.

Route & Requirements

The classic circular walk starts at the Länd car park in Scharnitz. A gentle gravel road takes you in about 45 minutes along the valley floor past the Scharnitzer Alm to the gorge entrance. The trail through the canyon is narrow, secured with sturdy wooden planks and wire cables, tracing the tumbling torrent directly above the water (approx. 45 minutes walking through the gorge). Surefootedness, a head for heights, and ankle-high boots with non-slip Vibram soles are essential, as the rocky path can be wet and slippery in places. The gorge is entirely unsuitable for pushchairs and bicycles. Beyond the gorge, the path leads to the cosy Möslalm hut or returns via a forest road back to Scharnitz (total loop 3.5 to 4 hours, 350 vertical meters, moderate). Pack plenty of drinking water and snacks in your rucksack.

Visit & Arrival

The gorge is safely accessible from mid-May to late October and is completely free of charge (closed in winter due to ice and avalanche hazards). Rail travellers reach Scharnitz easily aboard the hourly Karwendelbahn train from Innsbruck or Munich; the trailhead is about a 15-minute walk from the station. Motorists travel via Seefeld or Garmisch-Partenkirchen along the B177, parking at the Länd lot near the Scharnitz Nature Park Information Centre.

Tips

Rent an e-bike in Scharnitz to cycle effortlessly to the gorge entrance, lock your bike there, and hike through the ravine on foot. Stopping at the traditional Möslalm for Tyrolean grey cheese bread provides a rewarding conclusion to a refreshing walk.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Winterwanderung bei geräumtem Weg möglich)
